To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the conformational switch of the mRNA binding domain D5 of the ribosomal protein rS1 is the molecular basis of its chaperone activity.

the ribosomal protein rS1 is an essential protein in the translation initiation process, where the protein is able to bind to structured mRNA regions and unfold them to enable translation of the mRNAs.

1) the mRNA-binding domains of Vibrio rS1 form a unique architecture that covers a nucleotide binding length that is longer than previously thought; 2) D5 displays a conformational switch that is coupled with the order-to-order transition between two mutually exclusive secondary structure elements (β-strand- to α-helix) of a conserved ‘AERERL’ motif; 3) the conformational switch is exploited for melting structured 5’-UTRs
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of molecular mechanisms that control the initiation of translation.
the mechanism of how ribosomal protein S2 (rS2) and S1 (rP1) bind to the 5′-untranslated regions (5′-UTRs) of mRNA.
the mechanism of translation initiation in bacteria.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the rS1 protein has evolved a unique architecture that enables the protein to unfold structured RNAs by exploiting the conformational switching of D5.

the conformational switch of D5 in rS1 is an intrinsic property of this protein, and is used to compensate the entropic barrier of RNA-protein complex formation, which in turn is essential for efficient and fast translation initiation.
the conformational switch of the D5 domain of the ribosomal protein rS1 provides the structural basis for the unfolding of structured RNA elements in the TIR of bacterial mRNAs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ribosomal protein rS1 can act as a conformational switcher, which is essential to guide RNA unfolding during translation initiation.
we show how rS1 uses the conformational switching of D5 to guide unfolding of structured RNas for translation initiation.
we show that rS1 is a highly flexible protein, where the mRNA-binding domains are flexible and the D5 domain is flexible due to the conformational switch.
The main takeaway from our work is that
rS1’s mRNA-binding domains D3-D4-D5 are not only involved in the recognition and binding of structured RNA, but also in the unfolding of the mRNA.
the conformational switch between two alternative secondary structures is used for the melting of structured RNAs.
the conformational switch in S1’s D5 domain is essential for the efficient unfolding of structured RNA.
